page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.16-128 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors running at a sustained clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated physical cores corresponding to 32 vCPUs, implementing a single thread per physical core architecture rather than simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced resource ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

This server instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external block storage volumes or remote filesystems for persistent data operations. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and the configuration contains no GPU acceleration hardware. The dedicated single-threaded core implementation eliminates noisy-neighbor contention across virtual threads, supporting predictable performance for concurrent execution environments.

Featuring a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation, VM.Standard.A4.Flex.16-128 offers qualitative resource efficiency for high-density scale-out deployments. It is suited for containerized microservices, distributed continuous integration systems, application runtimes, and web serving clusters. Deployments requiring x86 instruction sets or high-speed local NVMe storage will require architectural validation or external network-attached storage architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.16-128 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors operating at 3.6 GHz, the configuration delivers 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core, eliminating hyper-threading resource contention. The system includes 128.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 4.0 GB per core resource allocation suitable for diverse operational requirements. It provides one complimentary public IPv4 address and contains no bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, necessitating external block storage for stateful environments. The dedicated ARM core allocation yields consistent compute throughput and predictable concurrency for multi-threaded processes. VM.Standard.A4.Flex.16-128 is well aligned with workloads including cloud-native microservices, continuous integration pipelines, web application hosting, and distributed container platforms that benefit from high core density and balanced memory capacity.
